title: Change a trach tube's inner cannula: draw the used one out along its curve, feed a clean one in to the click
instruction: Change the trach's inner cannula: put the used one in the red tray, then fit the clean one until it clicks.
context: LPNs (O*NET 29-2061.00, 0.6M US workers) 'assemble and use equipment, such as catheters, tracheotomy tubes, or oxygen suppliers'; respiratory therapists (29-1126.00, 0.13M) also change inner cannulas, every 8 to 24 h in long-term and home care. The cannula is a rigid curve: off its arc it jams and drags the tube out of the neck. The board's bayonet cap and push-until-click tasks are straight pushes; this one works only while turning about a centre 45 mm away. Steadying the neck plate with the other hand is allowed. A clean cannula that touches the table, tray or skin is contaminated.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Table: wood top, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Airway manikin, supine, head away from the robot, fixed, silicone skin: head 16 cm ball centred x 44, y 0, 8 up; neck 12 cm cylinder along x from 25.5 to 36.5, axis 4 up; chest x 10 to 25.5, 30 wide, 9 tall (5.5 at the sides). Size 6 cuffless tracheostomy tube in the neck at x 30, y 0: blue plastic neck plate 3.0 (x) by 8.4 (y) by 0.4, top 10.9 up; white 15 mm connector, 16.5 mm outside, 11.5 mm mouth, standing 0.8 above the plate, top 11.7 up, with a 27 mm retaining lip 2 mm thick just under its top; under it, inside the neck, the blue outer cannula, a round tube, 9.5 mm bore, 13.5 mm outside, curving toward the chest at 45 mm radius about x 25.5, 11.7 up. The outer tube weighs 20 g and is held down by ties (200 N/m); it can lift up to 12 mm. Two identical inner cannulas, 30 g each, loose: rigid tube 8.5 mm outside, a quarter circle of 45 mm radius (71 mm long); teal hub disc 21 mm across, 6 mm thick; teal grip fin 18 by 14 by 22 mm above the hub; teal sprung squeeze lever 6 mm wide in a slot in the fin, its paddle standing 9 mm proud of the fin's head-side face, its nose hooking 1 mm under the connector's lip (squeezed flush with the fin, 0.45 rad, the nose swings clear). Used cannula (cream tube): seated and latched in the connector, lever toward the head. Clean cannula (pale grey tube): hanging upright in the stand, hub face at x 31, y -10, 5.6 up, lever toward the head, tube down in the slot. Stand: light blue plastic, two walls 0.6 thick, 7 long, 5.6 tall, 1.3 apart, x 25.2 to 32.3, centred y -10, closed at the near end. Waste tray: red plastic, 14 (x) by 11 (y) by 3 tall, walls 0.3, centred x 19, y -22.5.
scoring: Grippers open. Seated: clean hub face within 2 mm of the connector top, axis within 5 degrees. Latched: seated, lever within 0.08 rad of shut. In tray: used cannula wholly inside the red tray's walls, below its rim. On manikin: any part of the used one over the chest (x 10 to 25.5, |y| up to 15) or neck and head (x 25.5 to 52, |y| up to 8). Released: every finger point 3 cm from both cannulas and the neck plate, both under 1 cm/s for 1 s. Whole-run, score 0: D, neck plate lifted 5 mm; C, clean cannula within 2 mm of the table, red tray or manikin skin. If released: 1.0 latched, used in tray; 0.75 latched, used on table or stand; 0.5 latched, used on manikin; 0.4 clean in but not latched (hub within 25 mm and 30 degrees of seated), used in tray; 0.25 used in tray, clean not in (a straight push jams 62 mm out); 0 otherwise. Ruler: plate lift, hub gap; photo: lever.
reset_notes: Take the fitted cannula out along its curve and hang it in the stand, lever toward the head; seat the other in the connector until its lever clicks under the lip. Check the neck plate sits down on its ties. Nothing is consumed: the two cannulas swap roles.
fidelity: Approximate. Real sizes: 8.5 mm cannula, 45 mm arc, 16.5 mm connector. The outer cannula is a round curved tube with 0.5 mm play per side (real about 0.3); a straight push jams 8.5 mm in. The cannula is rigid, like reusable ones, and 30 g (real about 5). One sprung lever stands in for two squeeze tabs. Ties are a 200 N/m slide. As in a real trial, scoring needs the grippers open and away: a finger within 3 cm scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: no score (the model refused the instruction before acting, see no_model_video_reason); demo: 1.0 (right arm moved used cannula to tray, fitted clean one, retreated)
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 was run through Inspect Robots on this task and refused the instruction before acting, so there is no recording: "PolicyError: DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction, refused: Performing invasive medical procedures like changing a tracheostomy cannula can hurt someone." (3 attempts on 2026-11-14, the last attempt with this error).
